   Executive verdict
   Yes: the agents are following the intended mathematical route, and the work since Tuesday is
   mostly productive. The important correction is that the current Phase 3 / Phase 5 "blocked" state is
   not merely a scheduler label. Both runs 122 and 123 independently identify the same genuine
   structural gap: the missing arbitrary-affine, family-level native presentation and cartesian base-
   change package needed to turn pointwise rank-one data into the public PicRankOneOpen /
   FibrePresented interface. That shared producer should now become the single critical-path task.



Short reply you can send

   Thanks - I had a look at the AJCR.review-plan, the current Phase 3/4/5 notes, the latest reports in runs
   121/122/123, and the relevant commits. My reading is that the execution is following the plan well, and I
   would not change the mathematical route.
   The main point I would clarify is the meaning of the present blockers. In Phase 3 and Phase 5 this is a real
   shared blocker, not just an item waiting in a queue: the agents have reached the same missing arbitrary-
   affine family-level presentation/base-change interface. Run 122 has the public rank-one locus side essentially
   kernel-clean; run 123 has completed a genuine separably-closed translated-cover feeder; but neither can
   honestly manufacture the missing PicRankOneNativePresentation/FibrePresented producer from fieldwise
   h0=1 and H1=0. I agree with their decision not to hide that gap behind a wrapper or switch to the high-
   degree/Galois fallback routes.
   So I would now concentrate one lane (probably the Phase-4/recovery lane, or a new lane with the right write
   scope) entirely on that family-level producer, and park 122/123 until it lands. Once that package is in place,
   the intended chain PicRankOneOpen -> canonical inverse/rankOneAbelIso -> translated cover -> Pic^0
   representability should start moving again. I would also encode this shared dependency explicitly in the
   roadmap, because Phase 3 and Phase 5 currently look independent in metadata even though their reports
   show they are blocked by the same theorem family.

Bottom line: keep the route; stop duplicating blocker discovery; give the shared family-level producer one
clear owner and acceptance contract.

The key interpretation of "blocked"
   Phase 3 is not blocked because the agent merely chose to work elsewhere. Its live roadmap contract asks
    for openness, arbitrary base change, and one public good-locus API; the current item is explicitly marked
    blocked. [R2]
   Run 122 says the gap is structural: the consumers already demand the exact arbitrary-affine native-
    presentation contract, but there is no lawful producer in the lane's writable boundary. [R5]
   Phase 5 says the same thing from the other side: the remaining blocker is a production arbitrary-affine
    presentation family with cartesian pushforward/base-change control, tied H0/H1/rank data, and coherent
    native presentations on every affine pullback. [R3]
   Run 123 then stops for the right reason: producing this requires protected Phase 3/4 integration; a
    fieldwise substitute would violate the requested API contract. [R6]

    Supervisory conclusion
    The blocker is shared and substantive. The dashboard status is therefore informative: downstream feeder
    work has succeeded, but the proof architecture cannot cross from fibrewise/fieldwise rank-one witnesses to a
    family-level morphism of functors until the arbitrary-affine base-change package exists.

The three lanes are independently converging on the same missing contract. That is usually evidence that
the architecture is now exposing a genuine bottleneck rather than that the agents are confused. The mistake
would be to leave the bottleneck implicit and let each lane spend cycles re-proving that it exists.

3. Why the blocker is mathematically the right one
At a mathematical level, the gap is exactly the passage from pointwise/fibrewise information to a family
construction. Knowing that a line bundle has h0 = 1 and H1 = 0 after passing to fields is not, by itself,
enough to define the inverse Abel construction as a morphism on arbitrary test schemes.
   To construct a relative effective divisor canonically from a family of line bundles, the pushforward must
    behave as a rank-one locally free object on the relevant locus, not merely have one-dimensional fibres.
   The construction must commute with pullback. In Lean terms, the cartesian pushforward/base-change
    morphisms needed by the public API have to be IsIso in the precise hypotheses used by the family.

   The H0 rank-one statement and H1 vanishing must be tied to the same native presentation and
    transported coherently under arbitrary affine base change.
   Only then does the canonical section/evaluation divisor vary functorially and supply the inverse to the Abel
    map on the rank-one open locus.
   Consequently, a fieldwise translated-cover witness is a valid feeder, but it cannot replace the family-level
    representability/open-locus theorem. This is precisely why run 123 is correct to refuse that shortcut.

4. Concrete coordination changes I would make now
A. Give the shared blocker one owner
1.     Create a narrowly named task such as "arbitrary-affine rank-one presentation and cartesian base-change
       producer" with write access to the Phase 3/4 integration files.
2.     Assign run 121 / Phase 4 to it, or start one new lane with that exact scope. The owner should be
       responsible for A-F on the previous page, not for the whole remaining Jacobian proof.
3.     Park runs 122 and 123 once their handoffs are recorded. Reactivate them only when the producer lands or
       when they receive a genuinely independent, producer-facing sublemma.

B. Encode the dependency in Horizon metadata
This is the main coordination smell I would fix. The current Phase 3 and Phase 5 roadmap files both still
show depends_on: [], even though their own summaries/reports identify the same missing producer. [R2,R3]
      Make the shared producer a first-class roadmap/task node.
      Add explicit dependency edges from Phase 3, Phase 4 where appropriate, and Phase 5 to that node.
      Use the comments/inbox for local failure memory, but let the graph encode the actual blocking relation so
       new sessions do not rediscover it from scratch.

C. Tighten the next checkpoint
      Checkpoint success should be binary: does an arbitrary-affine producer exist and is it consumed by the
       public rank-one locus/canonical inverse?
      Require a narrow build plus axiom audit at the consumer root, as the parent plan already demands. [R1]
      Do not use token count, number of commits, or new helper declarations as progress proxies. The current
       runs have already done enough exploratory/audit work to know the bottleneck.
      Keep high-degree Abel quotient and early Galois descent behind the fallback guard unless the rank-one
       route is formally shown impossible under the current library, not merely difficult.

D. What should happen immediately after the producer lands
     1 Run 122 closes PicRankOneOpen / DivRankOneOpen openness and arbitrary base-change acceptance.
     2 Run 121 uses the same producer to finish the canonical arbitrary-test divisor and family-level rankOneAbelIso.
     3 Run 123 upgrades its already-landed translated-cover feeder through the actual public rank-one interface,
     instead of a fieldwise substitute.
     4 Only then activate Phase 6 (Pic^0 representability over the separable closure), followed by the shared finite-
     Galois descent capstone and JacobianData assembly.

       My recommendation in one sentence
       No strategic reset is needed: turn the repeated Phase-3/5 blocker into one explicit Phase-4
       integration task, stop the two downstream lanes from spinning, and demand a consumer-closing
       arbitrary-affine base-change theorem family as the next milestone.

1. Executive summary
The project has made real progress, especially in widened divisor-family infrastructure, rank calculations,
and finite-Galois descent machinery. However, the current code growth does not yet correspond to
comparable movement toward the final Picard representability theorem. The central reason is architectural:
large divisor degree gives coverage but destroys Abel-map injectivity, while genus degree gives rank-one
uniqueness but is harder to cover over an arbitrary base field.

The recommended route is therefore AJCR-first and follows the curve-specialized classical construction:
build a rank-one Picard open over a separably closed field, represent it by an open inside the degree-g
divisor scheme, cover the Picard functor by translations of this open, then descend the resulting Pic^0
through finite Galois descent. AJC should be used as the shared descent engine and long-term infrastructure
project rather than as a second independent Picard proof.

  Primary decision
  The next endpoint-critical theorem is the family-level natural isomorphism between the rank-one open
  inside Div^g and the rank-one open inside the Picard functor. Parameter decoupling remains useful
  infrastructure, but it is no longer the main Picard endpoint lane.

2. The three principal issues
2.1 Coverage degree and injectivity degree are incompatible
On a genus-g curve, a nonspecial divisor of degree n has h^0 = n + 1 - g. At a sufficiently large admissible
degree, coverage is available, but h^0 is greater than 1 in positive genus. The Abel map then has positive-
dimensional linear-system fibres and cannot directly be the monomorphism or open immersion required by
the existing Picard chart seam.

At degree n = g, the same rank formula gives h^0 = 1 on the nonspecial locus, so uniqueness and an open-
immersion chart become possible. However, the required degree-g translation data need not exist over an
arbitrary base field. The project has therefore been attempting to make two different parameter regimes
solve one seam.

    Parameter regime                   What it gives                       What fails

    n=g                                Rank-one fibres; potential open     Pointwise coverage over the original
                                       immersion                           base field

    n = admissible > g                 Uniform coverage and large-degree   Injectivity; the Abel fibres have h^0 >
                                       control                             1




2.2 Lean interfaces are hiding mathematical misalignment
Several classifier layers use one symbol for distinct semantic roles: curve genus, divisor degree, and window
parameters. Equivalent geometric objects are also represented by different Lean expressions, causing
expensive definitional-equality and typeclass-search failures. Weak existential witnesses and source/test-
locus mismatches have allowed locally true lemmas to accumulate without closing the intended producer.

      Hard-coded diagonal relation n = g in classifier and RepresentableBy layers.
      Repeated transports between relCurve-style and explicit base-change expressions.
      Duplicate diagonal and generalized proofs surviving in parallel.
      Fieldwise uniqueness results used where the consumer needs a natural inverse on arbitrary test
       schemes.
      Compatibility wrappers that move hypotheses but do not create the missing geometric map.

2.3 The final theorem chain is not yet closed
The repository contains many strong components, but the final path is still discontinuous. The missing
central theorem is not another rank or coverage lemma; it is a family-level identification of the correct
divisor open with the correct Picard open, followed by a complete descent theorem returning both the

10. Phase 5 - Cover over a separably closed field
10.1 Translation theorem
Assume k is separably closed. For every extension K/k and every Picard class lambda on C_K, construct a line
bundle L0 on C/k such that the translated class has h^0 = 1 and h^1 = 0. The base-field origin of L0 is essential
because each translated open must itself be defined over k.

10.2 Formal proof strategy
5.    Twist by a sufficiently positive base-field line bundle until H^1 vanishes and H^0 is nonzero.
6.    If h^0 is greater than one, choose a k-rational point at which a nonzero section does not vanish.
7.    Subtract that point and use the exact sequence to lower h^0 by one while preserving H^1 = 0.
8.    Repeat until h^0 = 1.
9.    Return membership of the translated input class in PicRankOneOpen.

    theorem exists_translation_mem_picRankOneOpen
        [IsSepClosed k]
        (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
        (lam : picFunctor C (Spec K)) :
        exists L0 : LineBundle C,
          translate L0 lam in PicRankOneOpen C (Spec K)

16. Agent roles and dispatch specifications
16.1 Mathematical route reviewer
Read-only. Verifies theorem statements against the mathematical source, searches for counterexamples,
checks circularity, and classifies every blocker as mathematical, architectural, type-theoretic, or
performance-related.

16.2 Interface auditor
Creates minimal failing harnesses, parameter-role maps, and performance regressions. It does not write
broad production proofs or introduce new public APIs.

16.3 Vertical-slice builder
Owns one complete producer-to-consumer edge. A builder is not assigned a topic such as "work on Picard"; it
is assigned a theorem whose output is consumed by a named next theorem.

16.4 Merge and kernel reviewer
Checks root reachability, duplicate declarations, obsolete paths, axiom output, import cost, heartbeats, and
whether the new theorem is actually consumed.

16.5 Public API owner
One human or designated agent owns the public theorem signatures. Multiple agents may prove local
lemmas, but they may not create competing top-level interfaces.

     8	/-!
     9	# The canonical native rank-one presentation contract
    10	
    11	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` deliberately leaves the geometric producer fields explicit.
    12	This file fixes the module part of that contract: for a tied cocycle datum `D`, the module is
    13	always `D.nativeModule` and its base-ring comparison is always
    14	`D.nativeModuleKSheafIso`.  The native piece trivializations supply the line-bundle field;
    15	arbitrary-cartesian pushforward base change and the cohomology/rank certificates stay as
    16	explicit obligations.
    17	
    18	The resulting contract is therefore an adapter interface for a future producer, rather than a
    19	second choice of a line bundle.  Its conversion is consumed directly by the public
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter
    21	through this bridge, and the adapter itself does not provide the geometric certificates.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    30	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    35	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    36	
    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    38	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    39	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    41	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    42	
    43	/-! ## The native adapter contract -/
    44	
    45	/--
    46	A lambda-tied rank-one presentation whose module is canonically the native module of its
    47	cocycle datum.
    48	
    49	The fields after `datum_class` are exactly the remaining producer obligations.  The line-bundle
    50	certificate is derived from the canonical piece trivializations, so a field-level H⁰/H¹
    51	calculation or an unrelated line bundle cannot be silently substituted for the native
    52	evaluation module.
    53	-/
    54	structure PicRankOneNativePresentation
    55	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    56	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    57	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    58	  represents :
    59	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    60	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    61	  datum_class :
    62	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    63	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    64	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    65	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    66	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    67	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    68	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    69	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    70	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app datum.nativeModule)
    71	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    72	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    73	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    74	  h0_rank_one :
    75	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    76	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1
    77	
    78	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation
    79	
    80	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    81	
    82	/-- Convert the native adapter contract to the existing local-presentation contract.
    83	
    84	The two native bridge fields are inserted definitionally; all other fields are transported
    85	without weakening or adding hypotheses.
    86	-/
    87	noncomputable def toLocalPresentation
    88	    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    89	    PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam :=
    90	  { cover := P.cover
    91	    representative := P.representative
    92	    represents := P.represents
    93	    datum := P.datum
    94	    datum_class := P.datum_class
    95	    module := P.datum.nativeModule
    96	    module_iso := P.datum.nativeModuleKSheafIso
    97	    line_bundle := P.datum.nativeModule_isLineBundle
    98	    native_pushforward_base_change := P.native_pushforward_base_change
    99	    h1_vanishing := P.h1_vanishing
   100	    h0_finite := P.h0_finite
   101	    h0_projective := P.h0_projective
   102	    h0_rank_one := P.h0_rank_one }
   103	
   104	theorem nonempty_localPresentation
   105	    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
   106	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :=
   107	  ⟨P.toLocalPresentation⟩
   108	
   109	end PicRankOneNativePresentation
   110	
   111	/-! ## Immediate rank-one-locus consumer -/
   112	
   113	/--
   114	An arbitrary-affine family of native contracts supplies the existing public rank-one-locus
   115	consumer.  The family is quantified in exactly the same way as
   116	`PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition`; the conversion only canonicalizes the module
   117	choice and does not manufacture any of the remaining geometric certificates.
   118	-/
   119	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations
   120	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   121	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   122	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   123	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
   124	        Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
   125	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
   126	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   127	  apply mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi
   128	  intro A _ _ t
   129	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := h A t
   130	  exact P.nonempty_localPresentation
   131	
   132	end AlgebraicGeometry

    11	# Lambda-tied assembly of rank-one family certificates
    12	
    13	This file is the Picard-side consumer of `RankOneFamilyCertificates`.  It does not choose a
    14	module: the certificate and the native presentation are both attached to the displayed cocycle
    15	datum.  The cover representative and its equality with the displayed lambda class provide the
    16	Picard tie, while arbitrary-cartesian native pushforward base change remains a separate geometric
    17	input.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	set_option autoImplicit false
    21	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    26	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    29	
    30	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    31	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    37	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    38	
    39	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation
    40	
    41	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    42	
    43	/-! ## The literal native consumer -/
    44	
    45	/-- Assemble the native presentation from certificates for the same displayed cocycle datum.
    46	
    47	The equalities `hrep` and `hclass` tie the datum to the requested lambda class.  All four
    48	cohomological fields are projected from `cert`, whose modules are definitionally the H-modules
    49	of `D.sheaf`; no unrelated or pre-certified target module can enter.  The all-cartesian native
    50	pushforward comparison is intentionally an explicit argument until its protected producer lands.
    51	-/
    52	noncomputable def ofCertificates
    53	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
    54	    (x : descentClasses C E)
    55	    (hrep : PicEtAff.mk C E x = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1)
    56	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C E.Carrier pi)
    57	    (hclass :
    58	      (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) =
    59	        relPicMk C (overSpec k E.Carrier) D.cechPicClass)
    60	    (hpush :
    61	      ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    62	        (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of E.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    63	        (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C E.Carrier)
    64	        (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    65	          (relCurve C E.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of E.Carrier)) g),
    66	        IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app D.nativeModule))
    67	    (cert : RankOneFamilyCertificates D) :
    68	    PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam :=
    69	  { cover := E
    70	    representative := x
    71	    represents := hrep
    72	    datum := D
    73	    datum_class := hclass
    74	    native_pushforward_base_change := hpush
    75	    h1_vanishing := cert.h1_vanishing
    76	    h0_finite := cert.h0_finite
    77	    h0_projective := cert.h0_projective
    78	    h0_rank_one := cert.h0_rank_one }
    79	
    80	end PicRankOneNativePresentation
    81	
    82	end AlgebraicGeometry

     5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRankOneOpen
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneNativePresentation

     8	/-!
     9	# Conditional assembly of the rank-one fibre presentation
    10	
    11	This file isolates the final presheaf assembly.  It does not construct the still-missing
    12	arbitrary-scheme rank-one family or canonical evaluation divisor.  Instead, its input records
    13	native presentations on every affine pullback of one restricted family value, a natural
    14	evaluation-divisor classifier, and the classifier's geometric factorisation theorem.  From
    15	those inputs it constructs the stronger `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented` datum, proves the
    16	resulting square is a pullback, and feeds it immediately to
    17	`picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented`.
    18	
    19	Thus the declarations below are a conditional adapter, not the family-level producer required
    20	by the Phase-4 acceptance contract.  In particular, the divisor factorisation remains an
    21	explicit upstream obligation and receives no producer credit here.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    30	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    35	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    36	
    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    38	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    39	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    41	
    42	noncomputable section
    43	
    44	abbrev rankOneAmbient : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
    45	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
    46	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))
    47	
    48	abbrev rankOneLocus : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
    49	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
    50	
    51	abbrev genusDivisorYoneda : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
    52	  yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left
    53	
    54	/-! ## The explicit geometric input -/
    55	
    56	/--
    57	The explicit data needed to assemble one arbitrary-scheme rank-one fibre.
    58	
    59	`restrictedValue` is the restriction of the displayed ambient family to `W`, and
    60	`nativePresentation` quantifies over every affine pullback of that value.  The map
    61	`canonicalEvaluationDivisor` is the evaluation-divisor classifier on the rank-one locus, with
    62	its Abel compatibility kept explicit.  The last field is the unresolved geometric
    63	factorisation statement for that divisor, rather than a field of `FibrePresented` itself.
    64	Divisor uniqueness is not an extra hypothesis: it is recovered from Abel compatibility and the
    65	subtype inclusion.
    66	
    67	In particular, no field-fibre dimension witness, unrelated line bundle, or pre-existing
    68	`PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented` is accepted by this contract.  Conversely, this structure is not
    69	itself a producer: an inhabitant must still supply the arbitrary-affine native presentations and
    70	the canonical divisor factorisation.
    71	-/
    72	structure PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput
    73	    {X : Scheme.{u}}
    74	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C)) where
    75	  W : X.Opens
    76	  restrictedValue : rankOneAmbient (C := C).obj (op (W : Scheme.{u}))
    77	  restrictedValue_eq :
    78	    restrictedValue =
    79	      (yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) (𝟙 (W : Scheme.{u}))
    80	  /-- The tied native presentation on every affine pullback of the restricted family value. -/
    81	  nativePresentation :
    82	    ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    83	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ Over.mk restrictedValue.1),
    84	      Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
    85	        ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op restrictedValue.2))
    86	  /-- The canonical evaluation divisor classifier on the public rank-one locus. -/
    87	  canonicalEvaluationDivisor :
    88	    rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ⟶ genusDivisorYoneda (C := C)
    89	  canonicalEvaluationDivisor_abel :
    90	    canonicalEvaluationDivisor ≫ abelDivAffGenusSigma C =
    91	      picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi
    92	
    93	namespace PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput
    94	
    95	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    96	variable {g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C)}
    97	
    98	/-- The Sigma-extended public-locus inclusion is injective on every test scheme. -/
    99	lemma picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl_app_injective (S : Scheme.{u}) :
   100	    Function.Injective ((picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S)) := by
   101	  rintro ⟨a, x⟩ ⟨b, y⟩ h
   102	  dsimp [picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl,
   103	    CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat] at h
   104	  have hab : a = b := congrArg Sigma.fst h
   105	  subst b
   106	  congr 1
   107	  apply Subtype.ext
   108	  exact eq_of_heq (Sigma.mk.inj h).2
   109	
   110	/-- The public-locus element carried by the restricted family value over `W`. -/
   111	noncomputable def locusValue (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g) :
   112	    rankOneLocus.obj (op (F.W : Scheme.{u})) :=
   113	  ⟨F.restrictedValue.1, ⟨F.restrictedValue.2,
   114	    mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations pi
   115	      (fun A _ _ t => F.nativePresentation A t)⟩⟩
   116	
   117	/-- The map into the public locus is obtained from its universal element by Yoneda. -/
   118	noncomputable def fst (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g) :
   119	    yoneda.obj (F.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) :=
   120	  yonedaEquiv.symm F.locusValue
   121	
   122	/-- The canonical evaluation divisor of the restricted family value over `W`. -/
   123	noncomputable def evaluationDivisor
   124	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g) :
   125	    (F.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
   126	  F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op (F.W : Scheme.{u})) F.locusValue
   127	
   128	/-- The unresolved geometric factorisation of the canonical evaluation divisor through `W`.
   129	
   130	This predicate is deliberately separate from `PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput`: none of the
   131	native-presentation fields proves it. -/
   132	def CanonicalEvaluationDivisorFactors
   133	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g) : Prop :=
   134	  ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : rankOneLocus.obj (op S)) (w : S ⟶ X),
   135	    (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op S)
   136	        (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v) =
   137	      g.app (op S) w →
   138	    ∃ u : S ⟶ (F.W : Scheme.{u}),
   139	      u ≫ F.evaluationDivisor =
   140	          F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v ∧
   141	        u ≫ F.W.ι = w
   142	
   143	/-- The factorisation clause required by `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`, exposed without
   144	packaging it into that structure. -/
   145	def FibreFactorizationClause
   146	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g) : Prop :=
   147	  ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : rankOneLocus.obj (op S)) (w : S ⟶ X),
   148	    (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) v =
   149	      g.app (op S) w →
   150	    ∃ u : S ⟶ (F.W : Scheme.{u}),
   151	      F.fst.app (op S) u = v ∧ u ≫ F.W.ι = w
   152	
   153	lemma fst_comp_incl (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g) :
   154	    F.fst ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi = yoneda.map F.W.ι ≫ g := by
   155	  apply yonedaEquiv.injective
   156	  change (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op (F.W : Scheme.{u})) F.locusValue =
   157	    (yoneda.map F.W.ι ≫ g).app (op (F.W : Scheme.{u})) (𝟙 (F.W : Scheme.{u}))
   158	  dsimp [locusValue, picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl,
   159	    CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat]
   160	  rw [← F.restrictedValue_eq]
   161	
   162	lemma canonicalEvaluationDivisor_abel_app
   163	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g)
   164	    (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : rankOneLocus.obj (op S)) :
   165	    (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op S)
   166	        (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v) =
   167	      (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) v := by
   168	  have h := congrArg
   169	    (fun q => q.app (op S) v) F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor_abel
   170	  exact h
   171	
   172	/-- The family evaluation divisor has the displayed family as its Abel class. -/
   173	lemma evaluationDivisor_abel
   174	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g) :
   175	    yoneda.map F.evaluationDivisor ≫ abelDivAffGenusSigma C =
   176	      yoneda.map F.W.ι ≫ g := by
   177	  have heval :
   178	      yoneda.map F.evaluationDivisor =
   179	        F.fst ≫ F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor := by
   180	    apply yonedaEquiv.injective
   181	    rw [yonedaEquiv_yoneda_map]
   182	    rw [yonedaEquiv_comp]
   183	    have hx := yonedaEquiv_comp
   184	      (yonedaEquiv.symm F.locusValue) F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor
   185	    rw [hx]
   186	    simp [fst]
   187	  rw [heval, Category.assoc, F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor_abel]
   188	  exact F.fst_comp_incl
   189	
   190	/-- Once the divisor classifier and its Abel law are fixed, divisor factorisation is exactly the
   191	`FibrePresented.exists_factor` clause.  This equivalence records rather than conceals the hard
   192	geometric obligation. -/
   193	theorem canonicalEvaluationDivisorFactors_iff_fibreFactorizationClause
   194	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g) :
   195	    F.CanonicalEvaluationDivisorFactors ↔ F.FibreFactorizationClause := by
   196	  constructor
   197	  · intro hfactor S v w hvw
   198	    have habel :
   199	        (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op S)
   200	            (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v) =
   201	          g.app (op S) w := by
   202	      calc
   203	        (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op S)
   204	            (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v) =
   205	            (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) v :=
   206	          F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor_abel_app S v
   207	        _ = g.app (op S) w := hvw
   208	    obtain ⟨u, hud, huw⟩ := hfactor S v w habel
   209	    refine ⟨u, ?_, huw⟩
   210	    have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
   211	      (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.naturality u.op) F.locusValue
   212	    have htransport :
   213	        F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S)
   214	            (F.fst.app (op S) u) =
   215	          u ≫ F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app
   216	            (op (F.W : Scheme.{u})) F.locusValue := by
   217	      simpa [fst, yonedaEquiv_symm_app_apply] using hnat
   218	    have hdiv :
   219	        F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S)
   220	            (F.fst.app (op S) u) =
   221	          F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v := by
   222	      calc
   223	        F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S)
   224	            (F.fst.app (op S) u) =
   225	            u ≫ F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app
   226	              (op (F.W : Scheme.{u})) F.locusValue := htransport
   227	        _ = F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v := hud
   228	    apply picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl_app_injective pi S
   229	    calc
   230	      (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) (F.fst.app (op S) u) =
   231	          (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op S)
   232	            (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S)
   233	              (F.fst.app (op S) u)) :=
   234	        (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor_abel_app S (F.fst.app (op S) u)).symm
   235	      _ = (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op S)
   236	          (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v) := congrArg _ hdiv
   237	      _ = (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) v :=
   238	        F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor_abel_app S v
   239	  · intro hfactor S v w habel
   240	    have hvw :
   241	        (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) v =
   242	          g.app (op S) w := by
   243	      calc
   244	        (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) v =
   245	            (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op S)
   246	              (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v) :=
   247	          (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor_abel_app S v).symm
   248	        _ = g.app (op S) w := habel
   249	    obtain ⟨u, hu, huw⟩ := hfactor S v w hvw
   250	    refine ⟨u, ?_, huw⟩
   251	    have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
   252	      (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.naturality u.op) F.locusValue
   253	    have htransport :
   254	        F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S)
   255	            (F.fst.app (op S) u) =
   256	          u ≫ F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app
   257	            (op (F.W : Scheme.{u})) F.locusValue := by
   258	      simpa [fst, yonedaEquiv_symm_app_apply] using hnat
   259	    calc
   260	      u ≫ F.evaluationDivisor =
   261	          F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S)
   262	            (F.fst.app (op S) u) := htransport.symm
   263	      _ = F.canonicalEvaluationDivisor.app (op S) v := congrArg _ hu
   264	
   265	/-! ## Assembly of the stronger fibre datum -/
   266	
   267	/--
   268	Assemble the public fibre presentation from the native family and the canonical evaluation divisor.
   269	
   270	The divisor factorisation is a visible argument, and the preceding equivalence converts it to
   271	the exact public-locus clause.  The resulting pullback statement is therefore conditional on
   272	that unresolved geometric input.
   273	-/
   274	noncomputable def toFibrePresented
   275	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g)
   276	    (hfactor : F.CanonicalEvaluationDivisorFactors) :
   277	    PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g where
   278	  W := F.W
   279	  fst := F.fst
   280	  sq := F.fst_comp_incl
   281	  exists_factor := by
   282	    simpa only [FibreFactorizationClause] using
   283	      (F.canonicalEvaluationDivisorFactors_iff_fibreFactorizationClause.mp hfactor)
   284	
   285	@[simp]
   286	lemma toFibrePresented_W
   287	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g)
   288	    (hfactor : F.CanonicalEvaluationDivisorFactors) :
   289	    (F.toFibrePresented hfactor).W = F.W :=
   290	  rfl
   291	
   292	lemma toFibrePresented_isPullback
   293	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g)
   294	    (hfactor : F.CanonicalEvaluationDivisorFactors) :
   295	    IsPullback F.fst (yoneda.map F.W.ι) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g :=
   296	  (F.toFibrePresented hfactor).isPullback
   297	
   298	/-! ## Immediate openness consumer -/
   299	
   300	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_nativePresentations_and_divisorFactorization
   301	    (D : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
   302	      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C)),
   303	      PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi g)
   304	    (hfactor : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
   305	      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C)),
   306	      (D X g).CanonicalEvaluationDivisorFactors) :
   307	    PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi := by
   308	  apply picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented pi
   309	  intro X g
   310	  exact (D X g).toFibrePresented (hfactor X g)
   311	
   312	end PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput
   313	
   314	end
   315	end AlgebraicGeometry

    13	/-!
    14	# Descent-backed rank-one certificates for a tied cocycle datum
    15	
    16	This file is the cohomological half of the native family contract.  A certificate is attached to
    17	the displayed `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` and its displayed affine representative; it is never a
    18	certificate for a separately chosen module.  The only geometric input is the fibre witness
    19	condition (the mapped Čech class has a divisor with vanishing `H¹`), from which the datum
    20	dictionary and the rigid engine derive the three cohomological conclusions.
    21	
    22	The descent stage is essential: arbitrary coefficient rings need not be Noetherian.  We descend
    23	the finite cocycle datum to a finitely generated subalgebra, fire the engine there, and transport
    24	`H¹`, finite projectivity, and stalk rank through the on-the-nose datum H⁰ base-change
    25	equivalence.  Thus the public conclusions are genuinely arbitrary-affine, while the only
    26	Noetherian instance is local to the constructed stage.
    27	-/
    28	
    29	set_option autoImplicit false
    30	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    31	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    32	
    33	universe u
    34	
    35	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    36	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    37	open scoped TensorProduct
    38	
    39	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    40	
    41	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    42	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    43	
    44	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    45	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    46	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    47	
    48	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    49	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    50	
    51	/-! ## The actual fibre antecedent -/
    52	
    53	/-- A field-parametrised vanishing witness for the *displayed* cocycle datum.
    54	
    55	This is deliberately an abbreviation for the landed `HasWitnessH1Vanishing` predicate.  In
    56	particular its divisor has the class of this datum's cocycle; it cannot be replaced by a witness
    57	for an unrelated module or class.  The stage constructor below asks for this predicate on its
    58	finitely generated descent datum, where every stage residue field is an admissible coefficient
    59	extension. -/
    60	abbrev BasicOpenCocycleDatum.FibreH1Witness
    61	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi) : Prop :=
    62	  ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
    63	    [IsScalarTower k B L], D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L
    64	
    65	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    66	
    67	/-- The fibre witness is converted through the landed two-way datum dictionary. -/
    68	theorem subsingleton_pairH1_tensor_of_fibreWitness
    69	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi) (hW : D.FibreH1Witness)
    70	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
    71	    [IsScalarTower k B L] :
    72	    Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L) :=
    73	  (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L).mp (hW L)
    74	
    75	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    76	
    77	/-! ## The certificate object -/
    78	
    79	/-- The four cohomological certificates consumed by the native presentation.
    80	
    81	Every module in this structure is the H-module of the same `D.sheaf`; no native or unrelated
    82	module can be substituted. -/
    83	structure RankOneFamilyCertificates
    84	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi) : Prop where
    85	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1)
    86	  h0_finite : Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)
    87	  h0_projective : Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)
    88	  h0_rank_one : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
    89	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1
    90	
    91	namespace RankOneFamilyCertificates
    92	
    93	variable {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi}
    94	
    95	/- The standard base-change geometry is keyed by the structure morphism supplied by
    96	`relCurve.instOver`; re-key it locally so the rank theorem sees the same `Over` object. -/
    97	noncomputable local instance (priority := 20000) rankOneCertificateOver
    98	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    99	    (relCurve C L).Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
   100	  instOverBaseChange C L
   101	
   102	noncomputable local instance rankOneCertificateSmooth
   103	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   104	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   105	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   106	
   107	noncomputable local instance rankOneCertificateIntegral
   108	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   109	    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
   110	  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   111	
   112	noncomputable local instance rankOneCertificateQuasiCompact
   113	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   114	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   115	  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   116	
   117	noncomputable local instance rankOneCertificateFiniteH0
   118	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   119	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   120	  instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   121	
   122	noncomputable local instance rankOneCertificateFiniteH1
   123	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   124	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   125	  instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   126	
   127	/-! ## Canonical scalar extension -/
   128	
   129	/-- The canonical H⁰ equivalence attached to a certificate. -/
   130	noncomputable def h0BaseChange
   131	    (P : RankOneFamilyCertificates D)
   132	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
   133	    [IsScalarTower k B B'] :
   134	    B' ⊗[B] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ≃ₗ[B']
   135	      Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange B').sheaf 0 := by
   136	  exact D.datumH0BaseChange B' ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff D).mpr P.h1_vanishing)
   137	
   138	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   139	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   140	/-- H¹ vanishing is preserved by the same canonical coefficient extension. -/
   141	theorem h1_baseChange
   142	    (P : RankOneFamilyCertificates D)
   143	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
   144	    [IsScalarTower k B B'] :
   145	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange B').sheaf 1) :=
   146	  D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange B'
   147	    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff D).mpr P.h1_vanishing)
   148	
   149	/- The finite/projective instances for a tensor product are installed in the next constructor,
   150	   where they are used to transport the package's source module along `h0BaseChange`. -/
   151	
   152	/-- Scalar extension transports all four certificates, with the target still `D.baseChange`. -/
   153	noncomputable def scalarExtension
   154	    (P : RankOneFamilyCertificates D)
   155	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
   156	    [IsScalarTower k B B'] :
   157	    RankOneFamilyCertificates (D.baseChange B') := by
   158	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0
   159	  letI : Module.Finite B Q := P.h0_finite
   160	  letI : Module.Projective B Q := P.h0_projective
   161	  let e : B' ⊗[B] Q ≃ₗ[B']
   162	      Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange B').sheaf 0 := P.h0BaseChange B'
   163	  letI : Module.Finite B' (B' ⊗[B] Q) := by infer_instance
   164	  letI : Module.Projective B' (B' ⊗[B] Q) := by infer_instance
   165	  refine {
   166	    h1_vanishing := P.h1_baseChange B'
   167	    h0_finite := Module.Finite.equiv e
   168	    h0_projective := Module.Projective.of_equiv e
   169	    h0_rank_one := ?_ }
   170	  intro p
   171	  rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv e, Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange]
   172	  exact P.h0_rank_one (p.comap (algebraMap B B'))
   173	
   174	/-! ## The arbitrary-ring constructor -/
   175	
   176	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   177	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
   178	/-- Construct the certificate package after a genuine finitely generated descent stage.
   179	
   180	`hW₀` is the fibre-divisor/H¹ antecedent at the stage and `hdegree` is the corresponding
   181	class-degree calculation.  Neither field mentions the desired H¹/H⁰/rank conclusions.  The
   182	Noetherian instance is created only for `B₀`; the result is over the original, unrestricted
   183	ring `B` by the canonical datum base-change equivalence. -/
   184	noncomputable def of_descent_stage
   185	    {B₀ : Subalgebra k B} (hfg : B₀.FG)
   186	    (D₀ : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (↥B₀) pi)
   187	    (hbc : D₀.baseChange (B' := B) = D)
   188	    (hπ : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   189	    (hW₀ : D₀.FibreH1Witness)
   190	    (hdegree : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (↥B₀),
   191	      classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   192	        (D₀.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (genus C : ℤ)) :
   193	    RankOneFamilyCertificates D := by
   194	  subst D
   195	  letI : IsNoetherianRing (↥B₀) := hfg.isNoetherianRing
   196	  have hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (↥B₀),
   197	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D₀).H1 ⊗[↥B₀] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   198	    intro p
   199	    exact D₀.subsingleton_pairH1_tensor_of_fibreWitness hW₀
   200	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   201	  obtain ⟨h1₀, hfin₀, hproj₀⟩ :=
   202	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.descentRigidEngine hfg D₀ hπ hfib
   203	  have hpair₀ : Subsingleton (datumPair D₀).H1 :=
   204	    (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff D₀).mpr h1₀
   205	  have hrank₀ : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (↥B₀),
   206	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D₀.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   207	    intro p
   208	    haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   209	      instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   210	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   211	        (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘
   212	          Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   213	      instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   214	    haveI : QuasiCompact
   215	        (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘
   216	          Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   217	      instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   218	    haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   219	        (Sheaf.HModule
   220	          ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   221	      instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   222	    haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   223	        (Sheaf.HModule
   224	          ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   225	      instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   226	    exact BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one D₀ (n := genus C) hπ
   227	      (chi_moduleKSheaf C) hfib p (hdegree p)
   228	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule D₀.sheaf 0
   229	  letI : Module.Finite (↥B₀) Q := hfin₀
   230	  letI : Module.Projective (↥B₀) Q := hproj₀
   231	  let e : B ⊗[↥B₀] Q ≃ₗ[B]
   232	      Sheaf.HModule (D₀.baseChange (B' := B)).sheaf 0 :=
   233	    D₀.datumH0BaseChange B hpair₀
   234	  letI : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[↥B₀] Q) := by infer_instance
   235	  letI : Module.Projective B (B ⊗[↥B₀] Q) := by infer_instance
   236	  refine {
   237	    h1_vanishing := D₀.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange B hpair₀
   238	    h0_finite := Module.Finite.equiv e
   239	    h0_projective := Module.Projective.of_equiv e
   240	    h0_rank_one := ?_ }
   241	  intro p
   242	  rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv e, Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange]
   243	  exact hrank₀ (p.comap (algebraMap (↥B₀) B))
   244	
   245	end RankOneFamilyCertificates
   246	
   247	end AlgebraicGeometry

     7	/-!
     8	# The native module carried by a glued rank-one datum
     9	
    10	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sheaf` is already a sheaf of modules over the coefficient
    11	ring.  The presentation contract also asks for the same object as a sheaf of
    12	modules over the structure sheaf of the relative curve.  This file supplies
    13	that bridge: the componentwise `gluedQsmul` action gives a module on every open,
    14	`gluedRes_gluedQsmul` gives the semilinearity needed by
    15	`PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf`, and `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies its
    16	restriction to the coefficient ring with the original datum sheaf.
    17	
    18	The canonical piece trivializations also prove that the native module is a line
    19	bundle.  Pushforward base-change and existence of a tied
    20	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` remain genuine producer obligations.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    32	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    34	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
    35	
    36	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    41	
    42	/-- The structure-sheaf module on the sections of the glued datum over one open.
    43	
    44	The action is the componentwise multiplication action; the four module laws
    45	are inherited from the corresponding `gluedQsmul` identities. -/
    46	@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleOn (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
    47	    Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    48	      ((D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)).obj (op U)) := by
    49	  change Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    50	    (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U))
    51	  letI : SMul Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    52	      (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U)) :=
    53	    ⟨fun r s => gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s⟩
    54	  exact Module.ofMinimalAxioms
    55	    (fun r x y => gluedQsmul_add B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x y)
    56	    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_add_left B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    57	    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_mul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    58	    (fun x => gluedQsmul_one B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) x)
    59	
    60	/-- The presheaf of structure-sheaf modules underlying `D`. -/
    61	noncomputable def nativePresheaf : (relCurve C B).PresheafOfModules := by
    62	  let M : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat :=
    63	    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)
    64	  let family : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
    65	      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) :=
    66	    fun U => moduleOn D U.unop
    67	  letI : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
    68	      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) := family
    69	  exact PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf M (by
    70	    intro X Y f r m
    71	    change gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le
    72	        (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : X.unop ≤ X.unop) r m) =
    73	      gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : Y.unop ≤ Y.unop)
    74	        ((relCurve C B).resHom f.unop.le r)
    75	        (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le m)
    76	    rw [gluedRes_gluedQsmul]
    77	    apply Subtype.ext
    78	    funext j
    79	    rw [gluedQsmul_coe, gluedQsmul_coe]
    80	    simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom])
    81	
    82	/-- The native `Scheme.Modules` object associated to a glued datum. -/
    83	noncomputable def nativeModule : (relCurve C B).Modules := by
    84	  refine ⟨nativePresheaf D, ?_⟩
    85	  rw [show (nativePresheaf D).presheaf =
    86	    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat) from rfl]
    87	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    88	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    89	  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    90	    (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} B))).mp D.sheaf.property using 1
    91	  all_goals rfl
    92	
    93	/-! ## Piecewise line-bundle trivializations -/
    94	
    95	/-- Sections of the native module over one cocycle piece are the structure-ring sections.
    96	
    97	The open-immersion ring equivalence transports the component trivialization from the ambient
    98	relative curve to the restricted scheme.  The `gluedTriv_gluedQsmul` identity is exactly the
    99	structure-sheaf semilinearity needed for this to be a linear equivalence over the restricted
   100	ring of sections. -/
   101	noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv
   102	    (j : D.index) (V : (D.pieces j).toScheme.Opens) :
   103	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) ≃ₗ[
   104	      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) := by
   105	  let e := gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
   106	  let ρ := ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   107	  let f : Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) →ₗ[
   108	      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) :=
   109	    { toFun := fun s => ρ (e s)
   110	      map_add' := by
   111	        intro s t
   112	        change ρ (e (s + t)) = ρ (e s) + ρ (e t)
   113	        change ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t)) =
   114	          ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s) +
   115	            ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t)
   116	        rw [show gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t) =
   117	            gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s +
   118	              gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t by
   119	              exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).map_add s t]
   120	        exact ρ.map_add _ _
   121	      map_smul' := by
   122	        intro r s
   123	        change ρ
   124	            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
   125	              (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl) (ρ.symm r) s)) =
   126	          r * ρ
   127	            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s)
   128	        rw [gluedTriv_gluedQsmul]
   129	        simp [ρ] }
   130	  apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective f
   131	  constructor
   132	  · intro s t h
   133	    have h' := congrArg ρ.symm h
   134	    dsimp [f] at h'
   135	    rw [ρ.symm_apply_apply, ρ.symm_apply_apply] at h'
   136	    exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).injective h'
   137	  · intro r
   138	    refine ⟨e.symm (ρ.symm r), ?_⟩
   139	    change ρ (e (e.symm (ρ.symm r))) = r
   140	    rw [e.apply_symm_apply, ρ.apply_symm_apply]
   141	
   142	/-- The piecewise section equivalences assemble to a sheaf isomorphism with the unit module. -/
   143	noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSheafIso (j : D.index) :
   144	    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D) ≅
   145	      SheafOfModules.unit (D.pieces j).toScheme.ringCatSheaf :=
   146	  (SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _).preimageIso
   147	    (PresheafOfModules.isoMk
   148	      (fun V => (nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv D j V.unop).toModuleIso)
   149	      (fun {V W} f => by
   150	        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   151	        apply LinearMap.ext
   152	        intro x
   153	        change
   154	          ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso W.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   155	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le W.unop)
   156	                (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit
   157	                  ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop)) x)) =
   158	            (D.pieces j).toScheme.presheaf.map f
   159	              (((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   160	                (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x))
   161	        rw [gluedTriv_res B D.isGluingCocycle j
   162	          ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
   163	          ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x]
   164	        simp only [Scheme.Opens.ι_appIso]
   165	        change
   166	          (relCurve C B).resHom
   167	              ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
   168	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
   169	                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x) =
   170	            (relCurve C B).presheaf.map
   171	              ((D.pieces j).ι.opensFunctor.map f.unop).op
   172	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
   173	                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x)
   174	        rfl))
   175	
   176	/-- The canonical native module is locally a free rank-one structure-sheaf module. -/
   177	theorem nativeModule_isLineBundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle (nativeModule D) := by
   178	  intro x
   179	  let j := D.pieceIndex x
   180	  refine ⟨D.pieces j, D.mem_pieces_pieceIndex x, ?_⟩
   181	  exact ⟨nativeModulePieceSheafIso D j⟩
   182	
   183	/-- On every open, restricting `D.nativeModule` to the coefficient ring recovers
   184	the datum's original module of sections.
   185	
   186	The equivalence is the identity on sections. Its linearity is the substantive
   187	point: `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies the native structure-sheaf action
   188	of a coefficient scalar with the datum's coefficient action. -/
   189	noncomputable def nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv
   190	    (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
   191	    (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   192	      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) ≃ₗ[B]
   193	      D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) := by
   194	  let f :
   195	      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   196	        (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) →ₗ[B]
   197	        D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) :=
   198	    { toFun := fun x => x
   199	      map_add' := by
   200	        intros
   201	        rfl
   202	      map_smul' := by
   203	        intro r x
   204	        change gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U)
   205	            ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B U r) x =
   206	          r • (show D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) from x)
   207	        exact gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap B D.pieces D.unit
   208	          (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x }
   209	  exact LinearEquiv.ofBijective f ⟨fun _ _ h => h, fun y => ⟨y, rfl⟩⟩
   210	
   211	/-- The base-ring sheaf of `D.nativeModule` is canonically the datum sheaf.
   212	
   213	This has exactly the type of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.module_iso` when the
   214	presentation's native module is chosen to be `D.nativeModule`. -/
   215	noncomputable def nativeModuleKSheafIso :
   216	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   217	      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D) ≅ D.sheaf :=
   218	  (fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf _ _).preimageIso
   219	    (NatIso.ofComponents
   220	      (fun U => (nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv D U.unop).toModuleIso)
   221	      (fun {_ _} _ => by
   222	        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   223	        apply LinearMap.ext
   224	        intro x
   225	        rfl))
   226	
   227	end
   228	
   229	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum
   230	
   231	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# The rank-one evaluation zero-locus comparison
    10	
    11	The canonical inverse is cut out by the evaluation counit, while the existing divisor engine
    12	consumes the tied cocycle datum's local equations.  This file proves the section-level comparison
    13	between those two descriptions before any Noetherian or regularity hypothesis is introduced.
    14	
    15	For a tied local presentation, transporting a datum section through `module_iso.inv` commutes
    16	with restriction to every open.  Since every component of the sheaf isomorphism is injective,
    17	restriction vanishes on the module side exactly when it vanishes on the datum side.  Applying
    18	this to the canonical unit-lift through the evaluation counit identifies its restriction-
    19	vanishing predicate with that of `datumSection`.  The final theorem specializes the comparison
    20	to `PicRankOneNativePresentation`, whose converted module is definitionally the native module.
    21	
    22	This is a base-ring-linear section zero predicate, expressed through
    23	`toModuleKSheafOfModules`.  It is not an isomorphism of `O_X`-modules and does not identify the
    24	local equation ideals of the native line bundle.  That O-linear ideal comparison is still needed
    25	before the datum-side equations can be shown to cut out the intrinsic evaluation divisor.  This
    26	file also does not assert regularity, construct a family-level divisor, or manufacture the
    27	still-missing arbitrary-affine presentation producer.

    36	      Scheme.Modules.pullback g' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' :=
    37	  CategoryTheory.mateEquiv
    38	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f)
    39	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f')
    40	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫

    53	        Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫

    55	          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫

     9	/-!
    10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
    11	
    12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
    13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
    14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
    15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
    16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
    17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
    18	refinement.
    19	
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
    21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
    23	  `h` of covers.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
    25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
    26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
    27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
    28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
    29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
    30	  algebra.
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
    32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
    33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
    34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
    36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
    37	  descent datum.
    38	
    39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
    40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
    41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
    42	-/

    59	/-! ## Descent classes on an étale cover -/
    60	
    61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
    62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
    63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
    64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
    65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
    66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
    67	
    68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
    69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
    70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
    71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
    72	
    73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
    74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
    75	cover. -/
    76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
    77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
    78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
    79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
    80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))
    81	
    82	lemma mem_descentClasses_iff {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
    83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
    84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
    85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
    86	        = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x :=
    87	  Iff.rfl
    88	
    89	/-! ## Transport along refinement maps -/
    90	
    91	private lemma doubleInl_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
    92	    (doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
    93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by
    94	  ext x
    95	  simp [doubleInl]
    96	
    97	private lemma doubleInr_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
    98	    (doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
    99	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) := by
   100	  ext x
   101	  simp [doubleInr]
   102	
   103	/-- The descent condition is natural in the cover: pullback along a refinement map sends
   104	descent classes to descent classes. -/
   105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
   106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
   107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
   108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
   109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
   110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
   111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
   112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
   113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
   114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
   115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
   116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
   117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
   118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
   119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
   120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
   121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
   122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
   123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
   124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
   125	
   126	/-- Transport of descent classes along a refinement map of covers. -/
   127	def descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
   128	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C F :=
   129	  ((relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k)).comp (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
   130	    fun x => relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses C h x.2
   131	
   132	@[simp]
   133	lemma descentMap_coe {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   134	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
   135	    (descentMap C h x : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
   136	      = relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
   137	  rfl
   138	
   139	@[simp]
   140	lemma descentMap_id {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (x : descentClasses C E) :
   141	    descentMap C (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier) x = x := by
   142	  ext
   143	  rw [descentMap_coe,
   144	    show (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k = AlgHom.id k E.Carrier from rfl]
   145	  exact relPicAlgMap_id C _
   146	
   147	lemma descentMap_comp {E F G : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   148	    (h' : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
   149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
   150	  ext
   151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
   152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
   153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]
   154	  exact relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
   155	
   156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
   157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
   158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
   159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
   160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
   161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
   162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
   163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
   164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
   165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
   166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
   167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
   168	    ext y
   169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
   170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
   171	    ext y
   172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
   173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
   174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
   175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
   176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
   177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
   178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
   179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
   180	        rw [hx']
   181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
   182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
   183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]
   184	
   185	/-- **Refinement-map independence**: any two refinement maps between the same covers
   186	transport descent classes identically — what makes the plus construction independent of
   187	all choices. -/
   188	theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
   189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
   190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
   191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)
   192	
   193	/-! ## The plus construction -/
   194	
   195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
   196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
   197	the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
   198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
   199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   200	    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2
   201	  iseqv := by
   202	    constructor
   203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
   204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
   205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
   206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
   207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
   208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
   209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,
   210	        descentMap_comp, hfg', ← descentMap_comp]
   211	
   212	variable (A) in
   213	/-- The one-step étale plus of the relative Picard functor at the affine test `Spec A`:
   214	relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
   215	modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
   216	sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
   217	étale-separated — proved separately). -/
   218	def PicEtAff : Type u :=
   219	  Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))
   220	
   221	namespace PicEtAff
   222	
   223	/-- The plus class of a relative Picard class with a descent condition on a cover. -/
   224	def mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) : PicEtAff C A :=
   225	  Quotient.mk _ ⟨E, x⟩
   226	
   227	@[elab_as_elim]
   228	theorem ind {motive : PicEtAff C A → Prop}
   229	    (mk : ∀ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E), motive (mk C E x)) :
   230	    ∀ q, motive q := by
   231	  intro q
   232	  induction q using Quotient.ind with
   233	  | _ p => exact mk p.1 p.2
   234	
   235	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
   236	    {y : descentClasses C F} :
   237	    mk C E x = mk C F y ↔
   238	      ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier)
   239	        (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier), descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y :=
   240	  Quotient.eq
   241	
   242	/-- Transporting the representative to a finer cover does not change the plus class. -/
   243	@[simp]
   244	theorem mk_descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   245	    (x : descentClasses C E) : mk C F (descentMap C h x) = mk C E x :=
   246	  Quotient.sound ⟨F, AlgHom.id A F.Carrier, h, by rw [descentMap_id]⟩
   247	
   248	/-! ### The group structure -/
   249	
   250	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the left factor. -/
   251	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inl {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
   252	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
   253	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
   254	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)
   255	      = descentMap C f x := by
   256	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInl]
   257

# CHART-U(b) gap-2, the chartLocus-free core — fibre-field invariance of witness
h¹-vanishing (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 transport (ii), I-0252 gap 2)

CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii) (the "one `IsOpenMap` application", `Pic0ChartLocusOpen`
keystones 2/3) pushes the engine's open witness locus from the étale carrier `Spec B`
down to the test base `Spec A`.  Its remaining mathematical content (I-0252 gap 2) is
the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the preimage of the base locus with the
carrier locus: for a prime `q` of the carrier over `p`, the residue-field extension
`κ(q)/κ(p)` is separable (étale/étale-plus carrier) and must **preserve** the witness
h¹-vanishing of the fibre class.

That content is `chartLocus`-free (I-0252's phrasing through the still-undefined
`chartLocus`, DAT-C C9, is pure plumbing on top) and is landed here in the **witness
form** `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`
(`Pic0ChartLocusOpen`) uses.  The heart is a single module fact:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff` — for an `S`-module `H`
  and a field extension `L → L'` in the `S`-tower, `H ⊗[S] L` is subsingleton iff
  `H ⊗[S] L'` is.  Going up is `0 ⊗ = 0`; coming down is the faithful flatness of the
  (nonzero) field extension.  **Separability is not needed** — every field extension is
  faithfully flat; it is the geometric packaging (étale carrier) that makes the residue
  extensions separable, not the transfer.

Read through the two-way datum dictionary
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6) — under

  core**: witness h¹-vanishing of `D` at `L` transfers to and from `L'` for any field

          "body": "pic-c r4 SECOND INCIDENT: A CLEAN PRE-COMMIT STAT PROVES NOTHING WHEN THE SEED IS STALE, AND THE CAS DOES NOT SAVE YOU.\n\nMEASURED. 4e730419b9, reverted in cc03fff74c.
