      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

All rights reserved.\nReleased under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.\nAuthors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors\n-/\nimport AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.FiberBound\nimport AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.CurveBaseChange\n\n/-!\n# Extension-uniformity: the free half WITNESSED, and the open half reduced to one scalar\n\n`Ledger/FiberBound.lean` closes cluster-P items 1 and 3 over a *single* field `k`, and its\nclosing section says extension-uniformity splits into a free half and an open half.  That\nsection states the free half as a property of three **morphism classes**\n(`baseChange_binders_stable`: `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and\n`GeometricallyIrreducible` are each stable under base change).  That is true, and it is not\nthe same statement as \"the vanishing theorem re-fires at the base-changed curve\": a class\nbeing stable under base change says nothing until some object is exhibited carrying the\nbase-changed instances, in the spelling the consuming theorem actually elaborates against.\n\nThis file supplies the object.  `Scheme.baseChangeField C \u03ba` (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean`)\nis AJC's named base-changed curve `C_\u03ba = C \u00d7_{Spec k} Spec \u03ba`, and it already carries\n`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIntegral` as **named instances**.\nOne instance was missing from that stack \u2014 `GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is what the\n`Ledger` curve statements bind \u2014 and `geometricallyIrreducible_hom_baseChangeField` below adds\nit. /-!
# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map

`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.

The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
-/

/-!
# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus

An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
test and ties every piece of data to the input class:

* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.

No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.

+/-! ## The tied datum core -/

+/--
+The part of a native presentation that is forced by the displayed Picard value.

+`cover`, `representative`, and `datum` are not an alternative carrier: `represents` ties the

+structure PicRankOneNativeDatum
+    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
+  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
+  representative : descentClasses C cover
+  represents :
+    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
+  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
+  datum_class :
+    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
+      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
+
+namespace PicRankOneNativeDatum
+
+variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
+
+/-- Every displayed affine Picard value has a tied basic-open cocycle datum.
+
+The proof follows the actual representation chain: first expose an étale-plus representative,
+then choose a Cech representative of its relative Picard class, and finally refine that Cech class
+to the pinned basic-open datum.  No rank, vanishing, or base-change claim is made here.
+-/
+theorem exists
+    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
+    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) :
+    Nonempty (PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam) := by
+  have hplus : ∀ a : PicEtAff C A,
+      ∃ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E),
+        PicEtAff.mk C E x = a := by
+    intro a
+    induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
+    | mk E x => exact ⟨E, x, rfl⟩
+  obtain ⟨E, x, hrep⟩ := hplus (picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1)
+  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k E.Carrier)
+    (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))
+  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq
+    (C := C) (B := E.Carrier) (π := pi) c
+  refine ⟨{ cover := E
+    representative := x
+    represents := hrep
+    datum := D
+    datum_class := ?_ }⟩
+  calc
+    (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) = relPicMk C
+        (overSpec k E.Carrier) c := hc.symm
+    _ = relPicMk C (overSpec k E.Carrier) D.cechPicClass :=
+      congrArg (relPicMk C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) hD.symm
+
+end PicRankOneNativeDatum
